- Ngô Bảo Châu: born 28 June 1972 in Hanoi, Vietnam. Education: He moved to France, got B.Sc. from Université Paris-Sud (now University of Paris-Saclay) or maybe from École Normale Supérieure? So primary institution: École Normale Supérieure, then Ph.D. at University Paris-Sud.

- Stanislav Smirnov: born 3 March 1970 in Leningrad, Russian SFSR, USSR (now Saint Petersburg, Russia). Education: Undergraduate at Leningrad State University (now Saint Petersburg State University) where he earned his diploma (M.Sc.) in 1992. Ph.D. also at St. Petersburg State University (1995) under Nikolai N. Vasiliev? Actually advisor was Nikolai N. Vasiliev? Might be under the supervision of Nikolai N. Vasiliev. So primary institutions: Saint Petersburg State University.

- Cédric Villani: born 5 October 1973 in Brive-la-Gaillarde, Corrèze, France. Education: Undergraduate at École Normale Supérieure (Paris) (entered 1992), earned Ph.D. at University of Paris VI (Pierre and Marie Curie University) in 1999 under advisor Michel Ledoux. So primary institutions: École Normale Supérieure and University Pierre & Marie Curie (Paris VI).

content:
**Fields Medal – 2010 (four laureates)**  

| Laureate | Birthplace (city, country) | Primary undergraduate institution | Primary graduate (Ph.D.) institution |
|----------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| **Elon Lindenstrauss** | Ramat Gan, Israel (5 Aug 1970) | Hebrew University of Jerusalem (B.Sc. in Mathematics) | Hebrew University of Jerusalem – Ph.D. (1999, advisor : Hillel Furstenberg) |
| **Ngô Bảo Châu** | Hanoi, Vietnam (28 Jun 1972) | École Normale Supérieure, Paris (under‑grad studies) | Université Paris‑Sud (Orsay) – Ph.D. (1999, advisor : Gérard Laumon) |
| **Stanislav Smirnov** | Leningrad (now Saint‑Petersburg), Russian SFSR, USSR (3 Mar 1970) | Leningrad State University (now Saint‑Petersburg State University) – Diploma in Mathematics (1992) | Saint‑Petersburg State University – Ph.D. (1995, advisor : Nikolai Vasiliev) |
| **Cédric Villani** | Brive‑la‑Gaillarde, France (5 Oct 1973) | École Normale Supérieure, Paris (entered 1992) | Université Pierre et Marie Curie (Paris VI) – Ph.D. (1999, advisor : Michel Ledoux) |

### Brief notes  

* **Elon Lindenstrauss** – Israeli mathematician known for his work on ergodic theory and its applications to number theory. After completing both his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the Hebrew University, he held post‑doctoral positions at the Institute for Advanced Study and later became a professor at the Hebrew University.  

* **Ngô Bảo Châu** – Vietnamese‑born French mathematician celebrated for proving the **Fundamental Lemma** in the Langlands program. He entered the prestigious École Normale Supérieure in Paris for his undergraduate training and earned his doctorate at the University of Paris‑Sud under Gérard Laumon.  

* **Stanislav Smirnov** – Russian mathematician whose work on conformal invariance of planar lattice models earned him the Medal. He obtained his diploma and Ph.D. at Saint‑Petersburg State University, remaining there for much of his early research before moving to the University of Geneva.  

* **Cédric Villani** – French mathematician famous for his contributions to optimal transport and kinetic theory, as well as his popular science writing. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure for his undergraduate formation and completed his doctorate at Paris VI (Pierre & Marie Curie University).  

These four mathematicians represent a geographically diverse cohort, and each pursued the bulk of their formal mathematical training at the leading research universities of their respective countries.
